papers.title: Cost-Efficient Online Hyperparameter Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent work on hyperparameters optimization (HPO) has shown the possibility of training certain hyperparameters together with regular parameters. However, these online HPO algorithms still require running evaluation on a set of validation examples at each training step, steeply increasing the training cost. To decide when to query the validation loss, we model online HPO as a time-varying Bayesian optimization problem, on top of which we propose a novel \textit{costly feedback} setting to capture the concept of the query cost. Under this setting, standard algorithms are cost-inefficient as they evaluate on the validation set at every round. In contrast, the cost-efficient GP-UCB algorithm proposed in this paper queries the unknown function only when the model is less confident about current decisions. We evaluate our proposed algorithm by tuning hyperparameters online for VGG and ResNet on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet100. Our proposed online HPO algorithm reaches human expert-level performance within a single run of the experiment, while incurring only modest computational overhead compared to regular training.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究深度学习超参数优化，与FEA替代模型和生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA surrogate, no biomechanics, no structural simulation, no uncertainty quantification for physical systems.

summary_zh.motivation: 在线超参数优化每次训练步骤都需要验证集评估，成本高昂。
summary_zh.method: 提出代价反馈模型和成本高效GP-UCB算法，仅当模型不确定时才查询损失。
summary_zh.result: 在CIFAR-10和ImageNet100上达到专家水平，计算开销接近常规训练。
summary_zh.validation: 在VGG和ResNet图像分类任务上实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: Online hyperparameter optimization incurs high cost due to validation at each training step.
summary_en.method: Proposes a costly-feedback model and a cost-efficient GP-UCB algorithm that queries the validation loss only when the model is uncertain.
summary_en.result: Achieves human-expert performance on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet100 with modest overhead compared to regular training.
summary_en.validation: Empirically validated on VGG and ResNet image classification tasks.

papers.title: A Tailored Biomimetic Hydrogel as Potential Bioink to Print a Cell Scaffold for Tissue Engineering Applications: Printability and Cell Viability Evaluation
papers.abstract: The present study established a maximum standard for printing quality and developed a preliminary ideal index to print three-dimensional (3D) construct using the Gly-Arg-Gly-Asp (GRGD) peptide modified Pluronic-F127 hydrogel (hereafter defined as 3DG bioformer (3BE)) as bioink. In addition, the biocompatibility of 3BE for 3D printing applications was carefully investigated. For biocompatibility study and ideal printing parameter, we used the formulation of 3BE in three different concentrations (3BE-1: 25%, 3BE-2: 30%, and 3BE-3: 35%). The 3BE hydrogels were printed layer by layer as a cube-like construct with all diameters of the needle head under the same feed (100 mm/s). The printing parameters were determined using combinations of 3BE-1, 3BE-2, and 3BE-3 with three different standard needle sizes (Φ 0.13 mm, Φ 0.33 mm, and Φ 0.9 mm). The printed constructs were photographed and observed using optical microscopy. The cell viability and proliferation were evaluated using Live/Dead assay and immunofluorescence staining. Results showed that a stable of printed line and construct could be generated from the 3BE-3 combinations. Cytotoxicity assay indicated that the 3BE hydrogels possessed well biocompatibility. Bioprinting results also demonstrated that significant cell proliferation in the 3BE-3 combinations was found within three days of printing. Therefore, the study discovered the potential printing parameters of 3BE as bioink to print a stable construct that may also have high biocompatibility for cell encapsulation. This finding could serve as valuable information in creating a functional scaffold for tissue engineering applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及人工智能，不适用于AI生物打印方向。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML methods used; no integration of artificial intelligence into any bioprinting stage.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估一种改性水凝胶作为生物墨水的打印性和生物相容性。
summary_zh.method: 制备三种浓度的GRGD修饰Pluronic-F127水凝胶，通过不同针头打印测试。
summary_zh.result: 35%浓度水凝胶打印结构稳定，细胞增殖显著。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微镜观察和Live/Dead染色评估打印质量和细胞活力。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the printability and biocompatibility of a GRGD-modified Pluronic-F127 hydrogel as a bioink for tissue engineering scaffolds.
summary_en.method: Three concentrations (25%, 30%, 35%) of the hydrogel were printed with different needle sizes at a constant feed rate to determine optimal printing parameters.
summary_en.result: The 35% concentration hydrogel produced stable printed constructs and supported significant cell proliferation over three days.
summary_en.validation: Print quality was assessed by optical microscopy, and cell viability was evaluated using Live/Dead assay and immunofluorescence staining.
